coverage: Issuer credit update
ratings_as_reported: Moody’s Aaa (Stable), S&P AA+ (Stable)
credit_view: OCBC issuer profile Positive (2), direction Neutral, bond curve Neutral.
summary: OCBC expects earnings and cash generation to support Apple’s large net cash position. Dropping the net-cash-neutral target gives Apple more flexibility to fund investment. Apple’s bond spreads were generally tighter than Alphabet’s and Amazon’s in the report’s 30 September comparison.
key_metrics: 3Q FY2026: USD 31.9bn free cash flow and USD 62.2bn net cash. Cash and marketable securities of USD 146.5bn against USD 84.3bn of reported debt.
risks: Watch for a more aggressive capital policy, memory and storage shortages, smartphone competition, US–China supply-chain disruption and App Store regulation.

coverage: Issuer credit and bond relative value
ratings_as_reported: Fitch A+ (Stable), Moody’s Aa3 (Stable)
credit_view: BOS direction Negative. Overweight the 2029 bond and 2029 sukuk. Neutral on the other bonds and sukuk cited.
summary: BOS viewed Aramco’s credit quality as resilient after stronger-than-expected 2Q2026 earnings. Receivables under the domestic price-equalisation mechanism weighed on reported cash flow. BOS expected settlement and strong refining margins to help cash generation.
key_metrics: At 30 June 2026: 0.39× gross leverage, 0.09× net leverage and 6.2% gearing. USD 61.1bn cash and equivalents against USD 12.5bn in short-term debt.
risks: Regional conflict and export disruption remain the main downside risks. Track receivables collection, capital spending and dividend commitments.

coverage: Issuer credit and bond relative value
credit_view: OCBC issuer profile Positive (1), direction Neutral. Underweight the specified USD 2042 and SGD 2039 bonds on relative value.
summary: OCBC analyses Temasek on an investment-company basis. Low leverage, dividend income and staggered maturities support credit quality. Temasek Holdings is the guarantor of the Temasek Financial (I) bonds discussed.
key_metrics: At 31 March 2026: SGD 518bn net portfolio value and SGD 25.5bn total debt, or 4.9% of portfolio value. FY2026 dividend income covered interest expense 23×.
risks: Portfolio concentration, valuation and liquidity of private assets, higher-risk investments and limited standalone financial detail.

coverage: Rating agency report
ratings_as_reported: S&P AAA (Stable), short-term A-1+
credit_view: Stable issuer outlook as stated in the report.
summary: S&P cites low parent leverage, liquidity and disciplined asset rotation. Its rating also reflects its assessment of the likelihood of extraordinary government support. Temasek Holdings guarantees the Temasek Financial (I) bonds.
key_metrics: At 31 March 2026: SGD 518bn net portfolio value. S&P’s adjusted loan-to-value was below 10%. Three largest holdings accounted for approximately 21–22% of adjusted portfolio value.
risks: Watch for sustained concentration, weaker portfolio credit quality, reduced visibility into private assets or a change in S&P’s assessment of government support.

coverage: Rating agency credit opinion
ratings_as_reported: Moody’s Aaa (Stable), standalone baseline credit assessment aaa
credit_view: Stable issuer outlook as stated in the report.
summary: Moody’s bases its credit opinion on the size and quality of the portfolio, reliable dividends and liquidity for debt service. Its standalone assessment is already at the highest level.
key_metrics: At 31 March 2026: SGD 518bn net portfolio value. DBS, Singtel and PSA International accounted for 22% of portfolio value.
risks: Market-value volatility, concentration in Singapore and aggressive investment or liquidity deterioration could weaken the standalone assessment.

coverage: Issuer excerpt from regional credit research
summary: OCBC reported a five-year Keppel issue in offshore renminbi and discussed the potential M1 transaction. OCBC’s funding concern in that transaction discussion applied to StarHub.
key_metrics: September 2026 issuance: CNH 1bn, five years, priced at 1.95%.

coverage: Bond issuance note from regional credit research
summary: OCBC recorded the September green bond issued by CMT MTN Pte. Ltd. and guaranteed by CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust.
key_metrics: SGD 400m fixed-rate green bond, five years, priced at 2.646%.

coverage: Sovereign excerpt from thematic strategy report
credit_view: BOS portfolio view Neutral as of the report date.
summary: BOS views China’s external balance sheet and foreign reserves as buffers against external funding stress. The report identifies weak property activity and local-government financing pressures as constraints on growth.
risks: Property-sector weakness, local-government contingent liabilities and further trade or technology restrictions.

coverage: Historical sovereign credit update
credit_view: BOS direction Neutral. Hold on four specified HKINTL issues as of the report date.
summary: BOS highlights Hong Kong’s institutions, diversified economy and fiscal and foreign-exchange buffers. The report discusses the implications of soft local demand and trade exposure for growth.
key_metrics: Real GDP grew 3.1% year on year in 2Q2025, compared with 3.0% in 1Q2025.
risks: Exposure to trade tensions and weak domestic consumption.

coverage: Historical sovereign credit strategy
credit_view: BOS sovereign credit direction Neutral, portfolio stance Underweight US Treasuries and duration as of the report date.
summary: BOS linked persistent fiscal deficits to larger borrowing needs and a potentially higher term premium. The portfolio call reflected duration and supply considerations.
key_metrics: FY2024 federal deficit was 6.4% of GDP. Gross debt reached 123% of GDP at end-September 2024, as measured in the report.
risks: A wider deficit and higher issuance could raise long-term borrowing costs.

coverage: DBS issuer review in Credit Week in Brief
credit_view: OCBC assessed capital and liquidity as sound after a mixed quarter.
summary: Weaker markets trading weighed on DBS’s third-quarter earnings. Fully phased-in common equity tier 1 (CET1) declined as risk-weighted assets rose, but stayed above the bank’s target range. Both liquidity and stable funding ratios exceeded regulatory minimums.
key_metrics: 3Q2026: SGD 2.81bn net profit (down 5% year on year). Fully phased-in CET1 was 14.0%, from 14.6% in June. Liquidity coverage ratio 146%. Net stable funding ratio 115%.
risks: Watch trading-income volatility and whether risk-weighted assets continue to grow faster than capital.

coverage: UOB issuer review in Credit Week in Brief
credit_view: OCBC flagged Greater China asset quality and thinner provisioning coverage.
summary: Third-quarter operating profit declined from the prior quarter and a year earlier. Credit costs eased, while provisioning coverage weakened. Fully phased-in common equity tier 1 (CET1) fell, and both liquidity and stable funding ratios remained above 100%.
key_metrics: 3Q2026: SGD 1.81bn operating profit (down 3% year on year). Fully phased-in CET1 was 14.0%, from 15.0% in June. Average all-currency liquidity coverage ratio 152%. Net stable funding ratio 112%.
risks: Watch Greater China asset quality, provisioning coverage and further erosion of capital headroom.

coverage: Issuer credit update and bond relative value
ratings_as_reported: Bonds covered in the report: S&P AA+, Moody’s Aa2.
credit_view: iFAST assessed Alphabet’s credit as strong despite rising leverage and judged the USD bonds fairly priced against peers at publication.
summary: Google Services and Cloud earnings support the credit profile. In Q3, spending on property and equipment exceeded operating cash flow for a second straight quarter. Debt, including leases, more than doubled from year-end 2025, while Alphabet still had net cash on the report’s basis.
key_metrics: 3Q2026: USD 51.4bn capex and negative USD 9.1bn free cash flow. At 30 September: gross debt including leases USD 150.3bn, trailing debt/EBITDA 0.81× and interest coverage 51×, per iFAST.
risks: Watch the spending trajectory, large infrastructure purchase and lease commitments, and the effect on free cash flow and leverage.

coverage: Issuer credit update and bond relative value
ratings_as_reported: Bonds covered in the report: S&P AA−, Moody’s Aa3.
credit_view: iFAST saw weaker credit metrics and viewed the priced equity financing as a buffer for bondholders.
summary: Meta’s advertising business remained a strong source of operating cash, while the AI infrastructure buildout pushed quarterly free cash flow below zero. The report highlighted USD 37.5bn of priced preferred issuance and common-stock forwards, with timing and proceeds varying by tranche.
key_metrics: 3Q2026: negative USD 2.2bn free cash flow on iFAST’s basis, which includes acquisitions and finance-lease principal. At 30 September: USD 82.4bn in cash and marketable securities, 0.31× net debt/trailing EBITDA, and about USD 825bn of off-balance-sheet commitments as tallied by iFAST.
risks: Watch the growth and timing of data-centre leases and other contractual payments, sustained negative free cash flow, and further litigation costs.

coverage: Fiscal Q1 2027 ended 30 September 2026 and the November US bond sale
ratings_as_reported: S&P AAA and Moody’s Aaa on the Microsoft bonds covered
credit_view: Strong debt service capacity with less free cash flow available after investment.
summary: Azure and the rest of the cloud segment supported operating earnings. Data centre investment reduced free cash flow, and leases increased debt. iFAST saw the USD 25bn US bond sale as manageable given the earnings cushion.
key_metrics: iFAST estimates for the 12 months to 30 September: USD 60.0bn free cash flow, USD 135.9bn capex, lease-adjusted debt/EBITDA of 0.65× and EBITDA/interest of 63.8×.
risks: Watch data centre leases as they commence, spending on shorter-lived hardware, and how much contracted cloud demand depends on OpenAI.

coverage: Q3 2026 results, corporate borrowing and USD bond review
ratings_as_reported: S&P AA and Moody’s A1 on the bonds covered
credit_view: AWS earnings support credit as leverage rises and free cash flow falls.
summary: AWS generated nearly two-thirds of group operating profit. Spending on AI capacity ran ahead of operating cash flow, and USD 48.1bn of financing raised debt in the quarter. iFAST found near-term liquidity adequate.
key_metrics: Q3 AWS sales rose 39.3% year on year to USD 46.0bn. iFAST estimates: negative USD 42.4bn trailing free cash flow, USD 294.7bn debt including leases, 1.60× debt/EBITDA and 23.28× EBITDA/interest.
risks: Watch further borrowing, the interest expense on the new debt, higher planned capex and payments on leases that have yet to start.

coverage: Q3 2026 results, equipment financing and USD bond review
ratings_as_reported: Issuer ratings cited by iFAST: Moody’s Baa1, S&P BBB and Fitch BBB+
credit_view: Starlink supports debt service, while AI expansion consumes cash.
summary: Starlink drove most of the quarter’s operating profit. The group returned to operating profitability but still spent more on property and equipment than it generated in operating cash. Its liquidity provided a near-term buffer.
key_metrics: iFAST estimates for Q3: USD 9.6bn operating cash flow and USD 19.59bn property and equipment spending. September cash and short-term marketable securities totalled USD 89.86bn, against USD 39.0bn of principal debt and finance leases.
risks: Watch AI customer concentration, short termination notices on some revenue contracts, and multi-year GPU payment obligations.

coverage: Q3 2026 results, capital spending, shareholder returns and USD bonds
ratings_as_reported: Issuer ratings cited by iFAST: S&P A− (positive), Moody’s A3 and Fitch BBB+
credit_view: Net cash rose ahead of a step-up in capital spending and shareholder distributions.
summary: High memory prices and demand for AI hardware supported operating cash flow. Longer customer contracts give some visibility into demand when new capacity starts, and iFAST found the cash position supportive of short-dated bonds.
key_metrics: Q3 free cash flow was KRW 42.1tn. September net cash reached KRW 98.7tn and borrowings were KRW 15.8tn. Management’s FY26 shareholder-return target was about KRW 100tn.
risks: Watch the durability of memory margins, the 2027 capex step-up and buybacks as new industry capacity comes online.

coverage: Full issuer rating action commentary and FY2026–FY2029 rating case
ratings_as_reported: Long-term issuer default and senior unsecured ratings upgraded from BBB+ to A−, positive outlook
credit_view: AI chip growth and recurring infrastructure software revenue improve leverage.
summary: Fitch raised Broadcom’s rating after custom AI silicon and networking increased earnings, with VMware subscriptions supporting recurring cash flow. Outsourced manufacturing limits capital intensity and gives the company flexibility as investment and acquisition needs change.
key_metrics: Fitch cites more than USD 15bn of FY2025 free cash flow after dividends and projects EBITDA leverage below 1.5× over its FY2026–FY2029 rating case.
risks: Watch dependence on a few major cloud customers, in-house chip design by those customers, supply execution and renewed debt-funded acquisitions.

coverage: Full issuer rating action commentary following debt repayments
ratings_as_reported: Long-term issuer default and senior unsecured ratings upgraded from BBB to BBB+, stable outlook
credit_view: Debt repayments give Micron more room to absorb a memory downturn.
summary: Strong AI-related memory demand and pricing generated cash to retire debt. Fitch saw longer-term supply agreements as helpful for planning capacity, while retaining a cautious view of the industry's investment cycle.
key_metrics: Fitch estimated roughly 0.1× EBITDA leverage after the tender, down from 3.3× at the 2023 peak. The report cites about USD 8.6bn in FY2026 note repayments and USD 2.9bn in post-tender debt excluding finance leases.
risks: Watch a supply glut as capacity comes online, pricing pressure, and the effect of trade restrictions on Micron’s customers and competitors.

coverage: Full issuer rating action commentary and rating-case projections
ratings_as_reported: AA− long-term foreign and local currency issuer default ratings, stable outlook
credit_view: Net cash and diversified operations provide room for investment through the cycle.
summary: Fitch saw conventional memory scale and progress in high-bandwidth memory supporting earnings. Consumer devices add a steadier revenue base, while cash generation gives Samsung flexibility to fund capex and shareholder distributions.
key_metrics: Fitch’s rating case projects gross EBITDA leverage around 0.1× and continued net cash. It treats acquisitions as event risk outside its forecast.
risks: Watch memory pricing as supply expands, high-bandwidth memory execution, competition in devices and the losses in foundry operations.

coverage: Full issuer rating affirmation and outlook for lithography demand
ratings_as_reported: A+ long-term issuer default rating, stable outlook
credit_view: Lithography leadership supports cash generation, with sales concentrated among a few chipmakers.
summary: Fitch expects ASML’s leading position in EUV equipment, exposure to both logic and memory, and disciplined expansion to sustain cash generation through a moderate downturn.
key_metrics: The four largest customers accounted for 61% of 2025 total sales. Logic represented 66% of 2025 net system sales and memory represented 34%.
risks: Watch export restrictions, customer concentration, changes in large chipmakers’ capex and the timing of investment in new factory capacity.

coverage: Fiscal Q1 2027 ended 30 June 2026 and USD bond review
ratings_as_reported: S&P A+, Moody’s A1 and Fitch A on the bonds covered
credit_view: Cash balances and access to equity help fund the AI investment cycle.
summary: The cloud business grew and quick-commerce losses narrowed, but accelerated infrastructure spending reduced free cash flow. iFAST saw adequate near-term funding capacity, supported by net cash and a post-quarter equity raise.
key_metrics: iFAST estimates for June: RMB 31bn net cash, negative RMB 44.7bn quarterly free cash flow, and roughly 7× trailing adjusted EBITA/interest. Near-term debt cited was RMB 28.2bn.
risks: Watch sustained cash outflows, Qwen operating costs and the pace at which customers pay for AI services.

coverage: Full independent credit analysis of financing commitments, based on fiscal Q3 2027 filings
ratings_as_reported: S&P AA affirmation on 18 August 2026 as cited by the report
credit_view: Customer financing exposes NVIDIA to more credit risk through guarantees and longer payment terms.
summary: The analysis traces how NVIDIA supports customers building AI capacity through guarantees, payment terms and commitments. The largest Ohio campus guarantee takes effect in stages and requires a tenant default and a recovery shortfall before NVIDIA pays.
key_metrics: The Ohio campus guarantees have a USD 105bn maximum across qualifying leases as they commence. Receivables were USD 81.0bn at 25 October 2026, up from USD 38.5bn in January.
risks: Watch delivery and guarantee activation, longer collection times and the ability of data centre customers to secure funding independently.

coverage: Full independent credit and financing analysis based on the 2 November 2026 S-1/A
credit_view: Compute costs and the mismatch between short-term contracts and longer-term capacity obligations dominate the funding picture.
summary: Compute and infrastructure costs grew faster than revenue between Q2 and Q3. The authors track how notice periods on short-term capacity overlap with replacement capacity that depends on funding and delivery.
key_metrics: Q3 revenue was USD 16.956bn and compute and infrastructure expense was USD 9.863bn. About USD 4.3bn of the USD 213.8bn conditional or terminable commitments was expected to fall due in the following twelve months.
risks: Watch capacity delivery, the ability to fund longer-term commitments and how quickly cash conversion improves as usage grows.

coverage: Full Taiwan national-scale issuer rating affirmation and two-year credit outlook
ratings_as_reported: twAAA long-term and twA-1+ short-term issuer credit ratings on the Taiwan national scale, stable outlook
credit_view: Cash generation supports higher capex and continued net cash in the agency’s outlook.
summary: Taiwan Ratings expects TSMC’s lead in advanced and specialty manufacturing and a wider mix of applications to support profitability. It expects operating cash flow and financial policy to leave the company in net cash as investment rises.
risks: Watch competition at advanced nodes and concentration of production assets in Taiwan. The agency expects overseas expansion to reduce concentration gradually.

coverage: Historical issuer and senior debt rating action after Q1 2024
ratings_as_reported: Aa2 long-term issuer and senior unsecured debt ratings, stable outlook at publication
credit_view: Cash held at the parent and diverse operating businesses supported the 2024 rating.
summary: Moody’s pointed to strong insurance operations, a large liquidity buffer and earnings from a range of businesses. The report also discussed volatility from large investment and reinsurance exposures.
key_metrics: Q1 2024 operating earnings were USD 11.2bn, up from USD 8.1bn a year earlier. Moody’s cited USD 30bn as an example of a parent liquidity level that would signal rating pressure.
risks: The historical rationale flagged equity holdings concentration, large insurance exposures and leadership succession.

coverage: Historical full February 2025 senior unsecured notes rating action and issuer rationale
ratings_as_reported: Aa3 on new senior notes and the issuer, stable outlook at publication
credit_view: Growing product sales and cash flow supported the debt rating.
summary: Moody’s cited the growth of diabetes, obesity and cancer treatments and the company’s financial policy. The new notes were intended to fund the Scorpion Therapeutics acquisition and general corporate purposes.
key_metrics: Reported FY2024 sales were about USD 45bn. Moody’s identified sustained debt/EBITDA below 1.75× as potential upgrade support and above 2.75× as potential downgrade pressure.
risks: The report identified concentration in diabetes and metabolic treatments, development setbacks, drug pricing and large debt-funded acquisitions.

coverage: Historical full issuer rating confirmation using FY2024 results
ratings_as_reported: AA issuer rating, stable trend at publication
credit_view: Retail scale and operating cash generation supported a stable credit assessment.
summary: The agency cited rising transaction counts, strength in grocery and health, and margin recovery. It expected cash generation to cover investment and ordinary dividends while allowing flexibility for shareholder returns or acquisitions.
key_metrics: FY2024 sales were USD 648bn and EBITDA was roughly USD 39bn. The agency identified debt/EBITDA above 2.0× on a sustained basis as a source of rating pressure.
risks: The report highlighted competition, mature core markets, international expansion risk and weaker consumer purchasing power.

coverage: Historical full parent-company rating confirmation using Q3 2022 financials
ratings_as_reported: AA (low) parent long-term issuer rating, stable trend at publication
credit_view: Diversified earnings, a large deposit base and strong capital supported the parent rating.
summary: The agency considered the wide retail and wholesale franchise an earnings strength. It rated the parent one notch below its intrinsic assessment of the main bank and judged the group’s operational complexity an ongoing risk.
key_metrics: At Q3 2022 the group had a 12.5% CET1 ratio and around USD 2.4tn in deposits. Net income for the first nine months was USD 26.7bn.
risks: The report flagged capital markets exposure, day-to-day risk controls and sustained weakening in earnings, balance sheet or franchise reputation.

coverage: Historical full issuer and senior debt confirmation following FY2022 results
ratings_as_reported: AA (low) issuer and senior unsecured debt ratings, stable trend at publication
credit_view: Membership income and earnings supported leverage through a period of cost pressure.
summary: The agency cited stronger-than-expected operating results and stable membership renewals. It expected warehouse investment and occasional special shareholder returns to absorb some cash flow.
key_metrics: The agency expected lease-adjusted debt/EBITDA to remain below 1.50×. It projected capex of USD 3.8bn to USD 4.0bn for its FY2023–FY2024 case.
risks: The report flagged inflation pressure on margins, slowing volumes and debt funding for occasional special distributions.

coverage: Historical full issuer rating action assessing government support and standalone viability
ratings_as_reported: A long-term foreign-currency issuer default rating, stable outlook, and bbb viability rating at publication
credit_view: Fitch’s 2021 issuer rating relied on expected state support.
summary: Fitch described the bank’s size, state ownership and past support as reasons for its view. It separately assessed the bank’s funding, liquidity, asset quality and capital as stronger than most domestic peers.
key_metrics: At Q3 2021, reported impaired loans were 1.5% and CET1 was 13.4%. The report estimated a loan/deposit ratio around 82%.
risks: The historical report flagged weaker support, increased policy-directed credit and a deterioration in real estate loans or loss buffers.

coverage: Historical full issuer rating confirmation using FY2022 results
ratings_as_reported: A (high) issuer rating, stable trend at publication
credit_view: Brand strength and cash generation supported the historical issuer rating.
summary: The agency cited successful price increases alongside volume growth. It expected liquidity and access to financing to give the company room to handle a potential tax payment.
key_metrics: FY2022 EBITDA was USD 13.6bn on the agency’s basis. It flagged sustained debt/EBITDA beyond 3.5× as a possible source of rating pressure.
risks: The report flagged the IRS dispute, higher variable-rate interest expense, competitive pressure and changes in consumer preferences.
